bib.title: ALFWorld: Aligning Text and Embodied Environments for Interactive Learning

question: Can an agent that learns abstract text policies in an interactive TextWorld mirror of ALFRED generalize zero-shot to visually grounded embodied household tasks better than agents trained directly in the embodied world?
hypothesis: Learning to solve tasks in abstract language, free of physical-world particulars, lets agents use semantic priors to complete embodied tasks in novel environments.
contributions: ALFWorld environment: the first parallel interactive text-based and embodied environment.
BUTLER architecture: an agent that learns high-level language policies that transfer to low-level embodied execution, with modular components.
Generalization: BUTLER trained in the text domain generalizes better to unseen embodied settings than agents trained from demonstration corpora or from scratch in the embodied world.

method.summary: ALFWorld pairs ALFRED (THOR) embodied tasks with PDDL-derived TextWorld text games. BUTLER has a text agent (BRAIN, Transformer Seq2Seq with pointer softmax, trained by DAgger imitation of a rule-based expert in TextWorld), a Mask R-CNN template state estimator (VISION) and an A*/API controller (BODY); it is applied zero-shot to the embodied tasks.
method.task: goal-conditioned interactive household tasks (text games and embodied ALFRED), six task types, goal description only (no step-by-step instructions)

datasets.name: ALFWorld (ALFRED subset, six task types)
datasets.split: train; held-out seen (known task instances, same rooms, different object locations/quantities/appearance); unseen (new instances in unseen rooms)
datasets.source: built on ALFRED (Shridhar et al., 2020) in THOR; 120 rooms (30 each of kitchens, bedrooms, bathrooms, living rooms); excludes slicing and portable-container tasks
datasets.preprocessing: each scene converted to PDDL and a TextWorld game; templated goals (two templates per task type sampled equally); human-annotated ALFRED goals used for eval only (66 unseen verbs, 189 unseen nouns); step-by-step instructions omitted

datasets.name: Mask R-CNN fine-tuning images
datasets.source: replayed ALFRED expert demonstrations in THOR, ground-truth instance segmentation
datasets.preprocessing: images balanced across room types so object-category distribution is uniform

models.name: BUTLER::BRAIN
models.architecture: Transformer Seq2Seq encoder/decoder (5 conv layers, single-head self-attention, 2-layer MLP encoder; 3-layer MLP decoder), context-query attention aggregator, GRU, pointer softmax
models.init_from: frozen pre-trained 768-d BERT embeddings (Sanh et al., 2019), tied input/output embeddings
models.layers: encoder: 5 conv layers + self-attention + 2-layer MLP; decoder: 2 attention layers + 3-layer MLP
models.context: observation queue of k=5 most recent unique observations plus o0

models.name: BUTLER::VISION
models.architecture: Mask R-CNN (COCO pre-trained) fine-tuned on ALFRED frames, outputs formatted by templates

models.name: BUTLER::BODY
models.architecture: A* planner over pre-built grid-map with receptacle viewpoints, open-loop motion primitives; ALFRED API with Mask R-CNN masks for manipulation

models.name: Seq2Seq
models.architecture: same agent trained with behavior cloning on pre-recorded expert demonstrations, no DAgger

models.name: BUTLER-ORACLE
models.architecture: BUTLER with ground-truth detections and teleporting controller (upper bound)

models.name: VISION (ResNet18) / VISION (MCNN-FPN) / ACTION-ONLY
models.architecture: unimodal state baselines: ResNet-18 fc7 features, Mask R-CNN FPN features, or no observation

training.objective: imitation learning with DAgger on rule-based expert actions (token-level generation); RL tried first and failed
training.batch_size: 64 sampled data points from replay buffer (10 games to collect transitions); recurrent: 4 consecutive transitions, first 2 for state estimate, last 2 for update
training.steps: update every 5 data-collection steps; max 50 steps per episode
training.seeds: 8 random seeds; best seed selected per split

other.training_speed_Table3: EMBODIED-ONLY 0.9, TW-ONLY 6.1, HYBRID 0.7 eps/s, batch size 10

inference.decoding: greedy token-by-token; beam search (width 10, top-5 candidates tried in rank order) only to recover after a failed action
inference.max_tokens: 20 tokens per action; 50 steps per episode
inference.samples: all successes averaged across three evaluation runs (Table 2); best of 8 training seeds selected

other.beam_search_not_used: during evaluation in training curves, only for reported table scores

metrics.name: success rate
metrics.definition: percentage of episodes in which the goal is completed

metrics.name: goal-condition success rate
metrics.definition: fraction of goal conditions satisfied, proposed in ALFRED (e.g. 1/3 for putting any potato on the countertop in a hot-potato task)

eval.protocol: agent chosen as best of 8 seeds by TextWorld eval per split, then evaluated zero-shot on seen and unseen embodied tasks; three evaluation runs averaged; no significance test

limits: Subset of ALFRED only: slicing and portable-container tasks excluded.
Template-based state estimator and pre-built grid map are strong prior assumptions; observations are template text, not learned captions.
Large TextWorld to embodied gap (40/35 vs 19/10); oracle still only 37/26.
TW-ONLY beats EMBODIED-ONLY only on unseen; EMBODIED-ONLY is higher on seen (Table 3).
Hardware, compute and wall-clock for training are not stated; no significance tests; selection of best of 8 seeds per split.
Section 5.1 says 100K training episodes, Appendix B says 50,000.
